findings.title: Permission check requires user to be both team admin AND owner
findings.body: The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` instead of `||`: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. The naming and the rest of the check (`!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`) imply the intent is "admin OR owner", so that either role can add guests to a team booking. As written, only users who are both admin and owner (effectively owners only, assuming owner implies admin) are granted access, which is stricter than the variable name and likely the intended UX.

findings.title: Duplicate-email and blacklist checks ignore email case
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` filters new guests with case-sensitive comparisons: `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. The blacklist list is lowercased, but the attendees list is not, and RFC 5321 mailbox names are case-insensitive. As a result a user can submit `Foo@Example.com` against an existing attendee `foo@example.com` and bypass the dedupe, or against a lowercased blacklist entry and bypass the block. Both comparisons should be case-insensitive (e.g. `.toLowerCase()` on both sides).

findings.title: Wrong guest list passed to sendAddGuestsEmails
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the original input `guests`, but `guests` can contain addresses that were filtered out (already on the booking or blacklisted) and never made it into `uniqueGuests` or the database. Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails` the branch `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` is used to decide whether an attendee is "new" (gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail`) versus an existing attendee (gets `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`). Because the input list is used instead of `uniqueGuests`, existing attendees whose email happened to also be in the input will be re-classified as "new" and receive a fresh `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of an `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Pass `uniqueGuests` (the actually-added emails) into `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

findings.title: Email-send errors are silently swallowed with console.log
findings.body: The handler wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails` in a try/catch that does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`. The actual error is discarded (no `err` passed), the level is wrong (`console.error` would be appropriate), and the function returns success to the client even though the user was told guests were added but no notification emails were delivered. At minimum, log the error object via `console.error` and consider re-throwing or surfacing a partial-failure response so the UI can warn the user.

findings.title: No transaction wraps DB update, calendar sync and email send
findings.body: The handler commits `prisma.booking.update` first, then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and finally `sendAddGuestsEmails`. There is no surrounding transaction and no rollback if the calendar integration or email send fails partway through, the new attendees remain in the database but are missing from the underlying calendar/video meeting and from the participants' inboxes. This produces a data-integrity inconsistency between Cal.com state and the third-party calendar/video provider. Either wrap the side effects so the booking update can be rolled back, or at minimum document that a partial failure leaves the booking in this state and add a recovery path.

findings.title: Hardcoded English message returned from handler
findings.body: The handler returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` with a hardcoded English string. Every other booking mutation in this router uses translation keys (e.g. `booking_confirmation_success`). The frontend toast logic in `AddGuestsDialog.onSuccess` already calls `t("guests_added")` and never reads `data.message`, so the field is currently unused, but exposing a non-i18n string from the API creates a contract that downstream consumers will rely on. Either drop the field or return a translation key consistent with the rest of the codebase.

findings.title: Subject crashes when booking has no attendees
findings.body: `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` if `attendees` is empty. While every normal booking has at least the original booker, edge cases (data backfill, attendees deleted manually, etc.) can produce a zero-attendee booking, in which case sending this email will crash inside `getNodeMailerPayload` and abort the whole `Promise.all` batch in `sendAddGuestsEmails`. Use a safe fallback such as `this.calEvent.attendees[0]?.name ?? this.calEvent.organizer.name` (or skip the name interpolation) before accessing `.name`.

findings.title: isInvalidEmail state not cleared after successful submission
findings.body: In the `addGuestsMutation.onSuccess` handler, `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` is missing. The flag is set to `true` when validation fails, but if the user fixes the input and the mutation succeeds, the dialog closes without resetting the flag. Because the dialog component lives inside `BookingListItem` and stays mounted, reopening the dialog later shows the "Emails must be unique and valid" error immediately, even though the input is empty. Add `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` in `onSuccess` (and ideally on cancel too, which is already done).

findings.title: No size limit on guests array in schema
findings.body: ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.min()`/`.max()`. Combined with the `MultiEmail` component, which lets the user add arbitrary rows, a malicious or accidental request can submit an enormous array that is then inserted via `createMany`, triggering a large number of calendar/email side effects in `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` and `sendAddGuestsEmails`. Add a reasonable bound (e.g. `.min(1).max(50)`).

findings.title: Empty/whitespace entries are not stripped before validation
findings.body: `handleAdd` runs `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` directly. `multiEmailValue` can contain blank rows (initial state is `[""]`, and the X control only deletes the entry but does not trim). The schema rejects the whole array as soon as one empty entry is present, so a user with one valid email plus an extra empty row is forced to manually delete the empty row. The dialog would be more forgiving if it filtered `multiEmailValue.map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)` before validating and submitting.

findings.title: Attendees can add additional guests to a booking
findings.body: `isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(a => a.email === user.email)` grants any current attendee the right to add new guests to the booking. In most scheduling products only the organizer (or a team admin/owner) should be able to invite additional participants, because adding guests changes who has access to a meeting link, video room, or recording. The check should likely be `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer)` (drop the `!isAttendee` branch) unless adding guests is explicitly part of the product design here.

findings.title: No tests cover the new addGuests handler or dialog
findings.body: This PR introduces a new public TRPC mutation, a new dialog component, two new email templates, and several new translation strings, but ships without any tests for the handler (permission rules, case-insensitive dedupe, blacklist handling, transaction/side-effect behavior), the AddGuestsDialog (validation reset, empty-row handling), or the email templates. At minimum add a handler test that covers: organizer happy path, team admin vs owner permission, attendee duplicate (case-insensitive), blacklisted email, empty guests array, and missing booking.
